title: Finite integral coefficients admit a condensed two-term finite free resolution
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and its valuation ring $O=\mathcal O_E$ with its valuation topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with the discrete topology and let $a:O\to A$ be a continuous unital ring homomorphism. Regard $A$ as an $O$-module through $a$. Write $\underline O(S)=C(S,O)$ and $\underline A(S)=C(S,A)$ for the condensed ring sheaves on the site of profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and use module objects over $\underline O$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. There exist an integer $r\geq0$, an $O$-linear surjection $q:O^r\to A$ and an $O$-linear map $\phi:O^r\to O^r$ given by a matrix with entries in $O$ such that $q$ is continuous, $\phi$ is a homeomorphism onto $\ker q$ with its subspace topology, and
$$0\longrightarrow O^r\xrightarrow{\phi}O^r\xrightarrow q A\longrightarrow0$$
is exact as a sequence of $O$-modules. For every profinite set $S$, applying continuous functions gives an exact sequence of abelian groups
$$0\longrightarrow C(S,O^r)\xrightarrow{\phi\circ-}C(S,O^r)\xrightarrow{q\circ-}C(S,A)\longrightarrow0.$$
In particular $0\to\underline O^{\oplus r}\to\underline O^{\oplus r}\to\underline A\to0$ is an exact sequence of condensed $\underline O$-modules. The assertion includes $A=0$, for which $r=0$ is allowed.

source.place: Finite free and finitely presented coefficient extensions: exactness of the condensed finite free resolution of a finite O_E-algebra

proof.text: If $A=0$, take $r=0$, and take the unique maps between $O^0=0$ and $A=0$. They have all the asserted algebraic, topological and sectionwise properties, including for the empty profinite set. Henceforth assume $A\ne0$.

source.place: Finite free and finitely presented coefficient extensions: exactness of the condensed finite free resolution of a finite O_E-algebra

proof.text: List the elements of $A$ as $b_1,\ldots,b_r$, with $r=|A|$, and define $q:O^r\to A$ by $q(x_1,\ldots,x_r)=\sum_i a(x_i)b_i$. This is $O$-linear for the specified action. It is surjective since $q(e_i)=b_i$. Each function $x\mapsto a(x_i)b_i$ is continuous: coordinate projection and $a$ are continuous and multiplication on the discrete ring $A$ is continuous. Finite addition on $A$ is continuous as well, so $q$ is continuous. Put $K=\ker q$, an $O$-submodule of $O^r$, with its subspace topology.

source.place: Finite free and finitely presented coefficient extensions: exactness of the condensed finite free resolution of a finite O_E-algebra

proof.text: Put $N=|A|$ and let $c=N!\cdot1\in O$. For each $b\in A$, among $0,b,2b,\ldots,Nb$ two terms agree, so $k b=0$ for some integer $1\le k\le N$. Since $k$ divides $N!$, $N!b=0$. Thus $cA=0$ and $cO^r\subseteq K$. Also $c\ne0$: $O$ is a subring of the characteristic-zero field $E$, an extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$.

source.place: Finite free and finitely presented coefficient extensions: exactness of the condensed finite free resolution of a finite O_E-algebra

proof.text: By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $O$ is a discrete valuation ring, in particular a domain and a principal ideal domain. Apply [lem-sc-dvr-saturation-line-smith-normal-form] to the finite free module $O^r$ and its submodule $K$. It gives an ambient basis $u_1,\ldots,u_r$, a basis $v_1,\ldots,v_k$ of $K$ with $k\le r$, and scalars $d_i\in O$ such that, after indexing the distinct ambient basis vectors first, $v_i=d_i u_i$ for $1\le i\le k$. Each $d_i$ is nonzero, since a basis vector $v_i$ is nonzero.

source.place: Submodule.exists_smith_normal_form_of_le, lines 492-510, applied to the kernel submodule; local-field hypothesis from lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr

proof.text: In fact $k=r$. Otherwise $c u_{k+1}\in K$ by step 3, so it is an $O$-linear combination of $v_1,\ldots,v_k$, hence of $u_1,\ldots,u_k$. Comparing the coefficient of $u_{k+1}$ in the ambient basis gives $c=0$, a contradiction. Define $\phi:O^r\to O^r$ by $\phi(x)=\sum_{i=1}^r x_i v_i$. Since the $v_i$ form a basis of $K$, $\phi$ is injective with image $K$. Thus the algebraic sequence is exact. Its columns in the standard coordinates are the $v_i$, so it is given by a matrix with entries in $O$ and is continuous, by finite addition and multiplication in the valuation topology.

source.place: Finite free and finitely presented coefficient extensions: exactness of the condensed finite free resolution of a finite O_E-algebra

proof.text: Write $P:O^r\to O^r$ for the change-of-basis map with columns $u_i$. Both $P$ and $P^{-1}$ are matrices with entries in $O$, so both are continuous. For $y\in K$, the inverse of $\phi:O^r\to K$ is explicitly $\psi(y)_i=(P^{-1}y)_i/d_i$, computed in $E$. Indeed $y=\sum_i x_i d_i u_i$ for unique $x_i\in O$, so this formula has values in $O$ and gives $\psi\phi=1$ and $\phi\psi=1_K$. Each coordinate is continuous as an $E$-valued function: multiplication by $d_i^{-1}$ satisfies $|d_i^{-1}t-d_i^{-1}t^{\prime}|_E=|d_i|_E^{-1}|t-t^{\prime}|_E$. Since its values lie in $O$, it is continuous into the subspace $O$ as well. The product topology now makes $\psi:K\to O^r$ continuous. Hence $\phi$ is a homeomorphism onto $K$ with exactly the required subspace topology.

source.place: Finite free and finitely presented coefficient extensions: exactness of the condensed finite free resolution of a finite O_E-algebra

proof.text: Fix a profinite set $S$. Postcomposition with $\phi$ is injective because $\phi$ is injective. If $g:S\to O^r$ is continuous and $qg=0$, then $g$ takes values in $K$ and is continuous into that subspace. The continuous map $\psi g:S\to O^r$ is its unique lift under $\phi$. Conversely $q\phi=0$, so this proves equality of image and kernel on continuous functions.

source.place: Finite free and finitely presented coefficient extensions: exactness of the condensed finite free resolution of a finite O_E-algebra

proof.text: For every $b\in A$, choose $t_b\in O^r$ with $q(t_b)=b$. If $f:S\to A$ is continuous, its fibres $S_b=f^{-1}(\{b\})$ are clopen, because $A$ is finite discrete. They form a finite partition, including possibly empty parts. Define $h:S\to O^r$ to be $t_b$ on $S_b$. For every open $U\subseteq O^r$, $h^{-1}(U)=\bigcup_{t_b\in U}S_b$ is open, so $h$ is continuous, and $qh=f$. This proves surjectivity on continuous functions. Steps 7 and 8 give the whole asserted exact sequence of abelian groups, with no nonempty assumption on $S$.

source.place: Finite free and finitely presented coefficient extensions: exactness of the condensed finite free resolution of a finite O_E-algebra

proof.text: Coordinate projection and assembly give inverse natural $C(S,O)$-linear maps $C(S,O^r)\simeq C(S,O)^r$. Finite products here are also finite direct sums: the coordinate injections and projections obey $p_i\iota_j=\delta_{ij}$ and $\sum_i\iota_i p_i=1$, section by section. Thus these identify the two free sheaves with $\underline O^{\oplus r}$. By [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] the target is the sheaf $\underline A(S)=C(S,A)$, with the $\underline O$-action induced by $a$. The maps commute with precomposition in $S$ and with this action, so they are morphisms of module objects as in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects].

source.place: Finite free and finitely presented coefficient extensions: exactness of the condensed finite free resolution of a finite O_E-algebra

proof.text: The sectionwise sequence is short exact also in the category of these sheaves of modules. Explicitly, a sheaf-module map into the middle term annihilated by $q$ has, on every $S$, the unique $C(S,O)$-linear lift furnished by step 7; uniqueness makes these lifts natural in $S$, giving the kernel universal property. For the cokernel property, if a sheaf-module map $t$ out of the middle term annihilates $\phi$, define its factor on $f\in C(S,A)$ by $t_S(h)$ for any lift $h$ from step 8. Two lifts differ by an element in the image of $\phi$ by step 7, so this is well defined. Choosing lifts of sums and scalar multiples proves additivity and $C(S,O)$-linearity; restricting a lift gives a lift of the restricted section, so these maps are natural. Surjectivity on each $S$ proves uniqueness of the factor. Finally $\phi$ is monic because it is injective on every $S$. Thus $\phi$ identifies the first term with the kernel of $q$, and $q$ is its cokernel, proving the claimed condensed short exact sequence.
